headline: BOTH ROUND-9 BLOCKERS ARE GENUINELY CLOSED AND I RE-MEASURED EACH ON THE SHIPPED CODE RATHER THAN READING IT. R9-B1: the class is now named from the HARM, the 22 artifact reads are enumerated from the AST with the unguarded list EMPTY (my own independent sweep of the eleven modules finds exactly 22 in the register's domain - 13 narrow reads plus 9 swallowing predicates - and I confirmed all nine predicates fail CLOSED, so a swallowed error stands the section down or is purely cosmetic and never becomes a plausible False); 32 of 32 surface cells exit 0 with non-empty stdout and the source named on all four; and the 18-of-32 differential against the round-9 engine reproduces EXACTLY as claimed and cell for cell (mode-000 stream 4, DIRECTORY 4, SPARSE stream 4, SPARSE receipt 4, SPARSE spec file 2 dashboard-only), with the two round-9-covered shapes alive on both engines. R9-B2 is PROVEN line by line: 4 lines byte-identical to 520badd carrying the 8 pre-existing literals, 1 modified (module count 9 -> 10 -> 11), 4 added (two round 8, two round 10), 9 bound-bearing lines - I diffed all four revisions myself. R9-B3's count is genuinely DELETED, the property holds at three revisions (zero unparseable, zero non-dict lines at 3743283, 1a0a52e and aaa6a58), and the only surviving numerals are inside the sentence explaining why a count cannot be evidence. Note 1's --json walk is TRUE and I verified it on FOUR real stood-down surfaces rather than on the model: exactly two numeric leaves, both shortfall counts. Note 5's frame law is exact at {0:5, 1:7, 2:9, 8:21, 32:69}. THE ITEM FAILS ON TWO REAL DEFECTS THE HARM-DERIVED CLASS STILL DOES NOT REACH, BOTH ON THIS ITEM'S OWN FOOTPRINT FILES, AND ON ONE MEASURABLY FALSE ACCOUNTING SENTENCE. (1) TWO OF THE THIRTEEN DECLARED SOURCES take BOTH dashboard surfaces to exit 1 with ZERO bytes of stdout when they cannot be read - .warp/entropy.py (entropy_series_owner, UNREADABLE_ENTROPY_OWNER) and .warp/validate.py (front_matter_parser, UNREADABLE_FRONT_MATTER_PARSER) - while the two metrics surfaces exit 0 and NAME them, which is the identical asymmetry, on the identical two surfaces, through the identical owner file that round 10 itself called the third member of the class. It reproduces with mode-000 and needs NO memory ceiling. The cause is that round 10 guarded the entropy CALL (entropy_report) and left the entropy IMPORT: .warp/dashboard.py:56-58 loads .warp/entropy.py at module level outside any handler and .warp/entropy.py:83 loads .warp/validate.py the same way, and the register cannot see either because _M10_R10_PRIMS enumerates thirteen read primitives and omits the module loader. (2) A FIFO at .warp/events.jsonl makes ALL FOUR surfaces HANG FOREVER - no output, no exit - because the round-10 module aligned itself with the support reader on PRESENCE (lstat) and omitted that reader's KIND TEST (metrics_readers.py:144 os.path.isfile), which is the one primitive that refuses this shape ten lines away in the same footprint. (3) The label-diff accounting publishes 15 APPEAR / 5 DISAPPEAR where instrumenting expect() at both revisions measures 18 / 8, and its universal 'EVERY ONE OF THE FIVE IS THE SAME ASSERTION RESTATED, checked one by one rather than claimed' covers five of eight members - I checked all eight and every one IS benign, so the substance is true and the sentence is not.

must_fix_before_live.severity: blocking - a REAL DEFECT with TWO members, both on this item's own footprint files, both UNDECLARED, and both the harm the class is named after
must_fix_before_live.summary: TWO OF THE THIRTEEN DECLARED SOURCES STILL EXIT TWO OF THE FOUR SURFACES WITH ZERO BYTES OF STDOUT, WHILE THE OTHER TWO NAME THEM CORRECTLY. MEASURED on a relocated engine, round-10 tree, NO memory ceiling applied: a mode-000 `.warp/entropy.py` exits `.warp/dashboard.py` and `.warp/dashboard.py --html` EACH 1 with PermissionError and ZERO bytes of stdout, while `.warp/metrics.py` exits 0 (3600 bytes) NAMING UNREADABLE_ENTROPY_OWNER and `--json` exits 0 naming it too; a mode-000 `.warp/validate.py` does the same, with the metrics surfaces naming UNREADABLE_FRONT_MATTER_PARSER. The SPARSE variants of both reproduce it with MemoryError under RLIMIT_AS 4 GiB. THE CONTRAST IS WHAT MAKES THIS NOT A BOUNDARY QUIBBLE: a mode-000 `.warp/intent_corpus.py` and a mode-000 `.warp/incident.py` - the other two owner modules - are handled correctly on ALL FOUR surfaces, named and exit 0. So the pass already has the honest answer for `an owner that will not load' (metrics_owner_reads._owner, which catches the whole Exception family and names the owner), two of its four surfaces already give it, and the failure is confined to the two owners the DASHBOARD loads itself. THE CAUSE IS ONE PRIMITIVE OVER FROM ROUND 10's OWN THIRD MEMBER. Round 10 found that `ONE sparse spec file took BOTH dashboard surfaces down with MemoryError through .warp/entropy.py, which .warp/dashboard.py (this item's own footprint file) delegated to with no handler' and guarded the CALL: `entropy_figures' now wraps `entropy.entropy_report(events=events)' in `except Exception'. It left the LOAD of the same owner sixty lines up in the same file: .warp/dashboard.py:56-58 `_espec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("warp_entropy", ROOT / ".warp" / "entropy.py"); ... _espec.loader.exec_module(entropy)' sits at MODULE LEVEL inside no handler, and .warp/entropy.py:83 `V = _load("warp_validate", ".warp/validate.py")' does the same for the second owner. Both raise before a single byte is written, out of the import that every dashboard surface performs FIRST - structurally the same position as R9-B1(b)'s `the one function every surface calls first'. WHY THE GATE RULE CANNOT SEE IT, which is the part that matters for the method: the register keys on `the primitive that touches the artifact' and its list is `_M10_R10_PRIMS = ("read_text", "read_bytes", "open", "read", "loads", "load", "listdir", "lstat", "stat", "scandir", "iterdir", "walk", "glob")' (scripts/selftest.py:18640-18641). A MODULE LOAD is a read of a file that none of those thirteen names, so the 22-site enumeration is complete over its declared primitive set and blind outside it - I re-swept the eleven modules with a wider set and found 40 further unguarded `spec_from_file_location'/`module_from_spec'/`exec_module' calls, of which these two reach a DECLARED SOURCE. THE SPEC CLAIMS THE PROPERTY THIS BREAKS, in its own words: AC3 requires that `a sibling owner that would not load' is INCOMPLETE and `renders nothing', that `a sibling owner that will not load names ITSELF rather than being charged to whichever source was being read', and that `NO NUMBER means NO NUMBER ON ANY SURFACE: the rendered text, the rendered cards AND the machine-readable output each carry the completeness verdict and the named sources'. On two of four surfaces there is no verdict, no name and no output. IT IS NOT DECLARED ANYWHERE: grepped, neither the manifest's residual list nor the spec mentions an owner module that cannot be IMPORTED, so this is not a reclassified residual - it was never classified. IT IS NOT A ROUND-10 REGRESSION EITHER: identical on the round-9 tree, which is exactly the standing of R9-B1(b) when round 9 blocked on it. THE FIX FITS: resolve the dashboard's entropy owner through metrics_owner_reads (which already has the handler and already names it) or wrap the two module-level loads, and add the loader primitives to _M10_R10_PRIMS so the register stops being blind to a class of read it does not enumerate. .warp/dashboard.py has no per-module bound in the assertion list beyond the 1000-line budget and sits at 489, so there is room.

must_fix_before_live.severity: blocking - a REAL DEFECT, the same harm with no exception at all, UNDECLARED, with the remedy already implemented in the sibling reader inside this item's footprint
must_fix_before_live.summary: A FIFO AT .warp/events.jsonl MAKES ALL FOUR SURFACES HANG FOREVER: no stdout, no stderr, no exit code. MEASURED on the round-10 tree: `.warp/metrics.py', `--json', `.warp/dashboard.py' and `--html' each ran past a 60-second and then a 25-second timeout with ZERO bytes written, and I had to kill them. This is the class's HARM (`exits all four surfaces printing nothing') with the mechanism removed - a blocking read raises nothing, so no handler and no exception name can reach it, which is why the round's own gate rule, keyed on exceptions, is structurally unable to see it. THE PATH IS THE ROUND-10 MODULE's OWN READ: .warp/metrics_event_stream.py:118-129 `read_stream' does `os.lstat' (a FIFO is PRESENT), falls through, and calls `Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")', which opens the FIFO for reading and blocks until a writer appears. THE HONEST ANSWER IS TEN LINES AWAY IN THIS ITEM'S OWN FOOTPRINT AND THE ROUND DELIBERATELY DECLINED HALF OF IT: the SUPPORT reader of the SAME FILE does `_present' by lstat, THEN `if not os.path.isfile(str(path)): read_incomplete("event_stream", ..., "the event stream path EXISTS and is not a regular file (%s)")' (.warp/metrics_readers.py:139-149), and only then reads - so the support pass stands a FIFO at that path down BY NAME while the loop reader wedges on it. The round-10 module's own docstring says presence is decided by lstat `the same primitive the accounted read uses and for the same measured reason' and that `the two derivations now say the same thing about the same artifact in the same run': they do not, on this shape, because the module adopted the PRESENCE primitive of the sibling reader and not its KIND TEST. The item has already reasoned about this entry kind elsewhere - the availability differential counts 29 pure availability losses `because the entry is a symlink, a FIFO or a socket the rule may not dismiss unread' - so a FIFO is a kind this pass classifies everywhere except at the one artifact path it reads whole-file. NOT DECLARED: no residual, assumption or spec sentence mentions a non-regular file at the stream path. NOT A ROUND-10 REGRESSION: identical on the round-9 tree (both HANG), which again is R9-B1(b)'s standing. WORSE THAN THE CRASHES ALREADY BLOCKED ON, in one respect worth stating plainly: an exit 1 with a traceback tells an operator what happened and a CI job fails; a wedged process writes nothing and never returns, so a gate run hangs with no diagnostic at all. THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE the sibling already carries.

The manifest's inventory of the ten GENUINELY NEW labels is exactly right (the six round-10 assertions, the note-1 walk, the housekeeping, the two engine-sync assertions the new module adds); its error is that it counts FIVE restatements when there are EIGHT. I DIFFED ALL EIGHT PAIRS CHARACTER BY CHARACTER AND EVERY ONE IS A RESTATEMENT OVER A LARGER DOMAIN WITH CLAUSES ADDED AND NOTHING REMOVED, so `no assertion was deleted or weakened' is TRUE - and each of the three omitted changes is described elsewhere in this same manifest, so they were made knowingly and simply not counted. This is the third consecutive round whose label-diff figure does not reproduce (round 8 invented it, round 9's reproduced, round 10's is wrong by three in both directions), and it is the item's own method lesson verbatim: a property exhibited over a convenient subset rather than enforced over the domain. Publish 18 and 8 with the three named, or drop the count and assert the property (`every disappearance has a survivor that contains it') mechanically. (b) A SECOND MEASURABLY FALSE SENTENCE, in the label that carries the declared-set binding. scripts/selftest.py:18756 states that `every other site names them as a literal tuple BECAUSE THE TWO DERIVATIONS MAY NOT IMPORT EACH OTHER'. They do, three times, in exactly the way the constant would need: .warp/metrics_read_accounting.py:83-87 loads .warp/metrics.py and binds `_sibling = _core._sibling', .warp/metrics_support_contract.py:48-52 binds `_is_str = _core._is_str', and .warp/metrics_support.py:38-42 binds `parse_iso = _core.parse_iso'. Nothing forbids it either: the declared rule is `one direction of dependency', and support -> loop is that direction, so binding ARTIFACT_READ_ERRORS (or loading metrics_event_stream.py by path with the pass's own `_sibling' idiom, which imports nothing but json and os and cannot cycle) would have been legal. THE BINDING ITSELF IS SOUND AND I VERIFIED IT IS EXHAUSTIVE - see gate_observed.declared_set - so only the stated REASON is false. Prove it or delete the clause.

spec_edit_ruling: THE SPEC EDIT IS AN HONEST STRENGTHENING AND I WENT LOOKING FOR A WEAKENING. The observability block now names the class FROM THE HARM (`AN EXCEPTION RAISED WHILE READING A RECORDED ARTIFACT, WHICH NO HANDLER NAMES, EXITS ALL FOUR SURFACES PRINTING NOTHING'), states the four declared classes, says KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit are deliberately outside them, states that the reads are ENUMERATED FROM THE AST with the unguarded list asserted EMPTY, and states that the assertions DRIVE THE FOUR REAL SURFACES - each of which I verified mechanically rather than read. It also adds the honest half round 9's reviewer asked for: `A STREAM THAT EXISTS AND CANNOT BE READ AT ALL IS NOT A SHORTER HISTORY EITHER', with the named shortfall on all four surfaces and the ABSENT stream staying complete, empty and silent. Nothing was deleted or narrowed: the 18/1 numstat on the spec is 18 added lines and one modified. TWO THINGS THE OWNER SHOULD SEE. FIRST, THE CRITERION IS STILL NARROWER THAN THE PROPERTY THE ITEM IS JUDGED ON, one level up from where round 9 found the same thing. Round 9's lesson was that quantifying over a recorded LINE let two non-line members survive; round 10 widened to a recorded ARTIFACT, and R10-B1's two members are DECLARED SOURCES that are not recorded artifacts - engine owner modules - while R10-B2's is a read that never raises at all. AC3's own prose already quantifies correctly (`a sibling owner that would not load ... renders nothing', `NO NUMBER ON ANY SURFACE'), so the criterion that the OBSERVABILITY BLOCK writes is the narrower of the two documents, and a class boundary drawn at `every SOURCE this pass DECLARES, however it is read, and whether the read raises or blocks' would have caught all three. SECOND, the block's sentence `EVERY READ OF A RECORDED ARTIFACT IN THIS PASS THEREFORE SITS INSIDE A HANDLER' is true of the register's thirteen primitives and silent about the module loader, which is the mechanism by which two of this item's own footprint reads escaped it - the sentence and the register agree with each other and both under-cover the code.
notes: Ranked by six-month impact. 1. THE REGISTER'S PRIMITIVE LIST IS THE NEXT TAXONOMY TO OUTGROW, and it is worth saying explicitly because this is the fourth consecutive round where the sweep's own key was the blind spot. Round 9 keyed on the MECHANISM (recursion) and missed two members. Round 10 keyed on THE PRIMITIVE THAT TOUCHES THE ARTIFACT and enumerated thirteen names - which is a genuine improvement and found both - but a primitive list is still a name list, and `exec_module' is not on it. My wider sweep of the same eleven modules found 40 further file-touching calls outside the register (spec_from_file_location, module_from_spec, exec_module, Path.resolve), two of which reach a DECLARED SOURCE and are R10-B1. The rule that would not need a list is structural: enumerate the SOURCES the pass declares (thirteen rows, already a table) and assert that every code path which can make one unavailable answers with that source's own name on all four surfaces - derived from the source table rather than from a vocabulary of primitives. That is checkable from the same AST and it would have failed on dashboard.py:56 immediately. 2. THE DELEGATION REGISTER IS BETTER AND STILL NAME-KEYED. Round 9's note 2 said `key the register on the owner namespace, not on six names'; round 10 replaced six call names with six call names plus six owner NAMES plus four owner ATTRS (scripts/selftest.py:18326-18328), found a genuine eighth site with it (the dashboard's entropy_report delegation, which was a real member of the class) and states EIGHT sites where the comment used to say seven while pinning six. So the mismatch round 9 found is fixed and the register is now honest about its own size - but it is still a hardcoded list of identifiers, so a ninth site that binds an owner to a name not on it is invisible in exactly the way the seventh was. I verified the eight are right: my own handler sweep finds ten Exception-family handlers, of which exactly two are not owner delegations (metrics.py parse_iso and metrics_event_stream.load_stream's json.loads, both pre-existing and both correctly excluded). 3. THE BROAD `Exception' IN entropy_figures IS JUSTIFIED, and I checked the specific worry that a programming error would go quiet. This pass already publishes a closed table of THIRTEEN SOURCES with a taxonomy name for each. A rule that quantifies over that table - every declared source, however it is reached, whether the failure raises or blocks, must answer with its own name on all four surfaces - needs no vocabulary of primitives, cannot go stale when a new one is used, and fails on both of today's members immediately. A rule that quantifies over primitives will always be one name short, and this is the third round to prove it. The second lesson is the one seven rounds have already taught and this round repeats in miniature: an accounting sentence is a claim, and 15 / 5 where the measurement is 18 / 8 is the same failure as 573 and 576 - the universal `every one of the five is a restatement' was checked over five of eight members, and it happens to be true over all eight only because I checked the other three.
